items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: Yes, we had Buddy Tate, Cat Anderson, Gene Ramey, Gus Johnson, the old rhythm section.

ctx.x: And you had a special band, didn't you?
Yes, we had Buddy Tate, Cat Anderson, Gene Ramey, Gus Johnson, the old rhythm section.
You didn't know him in Kansas City.

No. I didn't know Jay. Actually, Jay is from Muskogee and he's a little younger. So when I was around Kansas City, Jay hadn't come to Kansas City. Then my cousin wrote me, he wanted to come to New York. There's a trumpet player that played Jay and he asked me if he could come to New York, could I help him get into the union. So I told him, you know, he had to pay his dues that come into the six -- you know, had to actually do the six months just like everybody
else. So -- but he told me about this band, Jay McShann, and we started listening to a record. I think the record -- Bird was on it, called "Swingtism," something.

items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: Then come Jay McShann after, but they all had a different thing

ctx.x: So you say that feel is more relaxed?

More relaxed but still swing. It was more swinging. And they was just having fits and jumping and having fits, and they would be swinging, and those guys would be taking those fine solos and things behind them. And it just swept the whole thing away. It was Chick Webb, well Chick played everything, it had to be up here, you know? It’d be up there, they’d have the midwest swing. Then come Jay McShann after, but they all had a different thing, had a different thing. Andy Kirk had more of a sweet band, people like…

You know I spent some time in that area myself, when you talk about Tulsa, Oklahoma, I spent ten years in Tulsa. And I noticed that the feel is different. It’s more relaxed, it’s got a nice bounce to it, but it doesn’t sound so jumpy and hurried. And it’s still kind of like that.

items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Now you worked with some great Texas Tenors yourself, Buddy Tate? Some great recordings.

ctx.x: Well there’s a lot of places where I thought the people would never ever wake up. A lot of places he never made no impression at all. It was a horrible thing to say, but a lot of places he never made no impression at all. And some places he made an impression you know, made good impressions. They always loved Bird at the Savoy Ballroom. They loved Bird all over New York City. New York loved him. But it took him so long to decide, well what are we going to do about him, or what are we going to do with him. I…
Now you worked with some great Texas Tenors yourself, Buddy Tate? Some great recordings.
Yes Buddy Tate was one of them great Texas Tenors.
